title: Tin whistle
reference_instrument: a different whistle, with a count: a Waltons Irish ThinWhistle in D, one short note each at D5, E5, F#5, G5, A5, B5, C#6 and D6 (cernoel, Freesound pack 22189 'Waltons Irish ThinWhistle in D', CC0), each ruled by its neighbouring notes; the reference is a lossy MP3 preview (about 130-180 kbit/s), and each preview also holds a held take of the same note (about 1 s) beside the short one that is graded; the repo's screen marks the held take invalid for the noise-floor test (no lead-in before the onset, no stationary tail), so it does not rule. The F#5 file is titled 'F.wav'; the screen measures its short take at 732.5 Hz, 82 c above F5 and 17.7 c below F#5, and re-screens it as Gb5. It is not the modelled Clare whistle, and on these notes it reads +10.7, -22.9, -21.9, -6.3, -34.4, +24.6, +19.2 and +24.6 c from A440 equal temperament
summary: D5, E5, F#5, G5, A5, B5, C#6 and D6 are graded against single short notes of a different whistle, a Waltons D, each a lossy preview: 1 of 12, 3 of 12, 3 of 12, 1 of 11, 2 of 12, 3 of 12, 3 of 12 and 3 of 12 measures sit inside the spread between that whistle's neighbouring notes, and no note has a same-note ruler. With the paper's 0.3 mm tone-hole walls the eight notes sound D5 +9.1, E5 -4.8, F#5 -15.4, G5 -0.7, A5 -4.6, B5 +4.6, C#6 +5.4 and D6 +13.0 c from equal temperament (the bore's gas is breath, which sits about 11 c above the paper's dry air), and against the Waltons notes D5 1.6 c flat, E5 18.1, F#5 6.5, G5 5.6 and A5 29.7 c sharp, B5 20.1, C#6 13.8 and D6 11.6 c flat; before the walls, six of the notes sounded 21 to 35 c flat of their names. The harmonics don't follow the real one's. This is a Clare D whistle built from the ISVR measurements of one real whistle (Davies, Pinho and English 2006): bore, six finger holes, flue, window and pocket, blown at each note's printed air flow through a forced Bickley jet. It carries Fletcher's 1976 jet spreading as a trial, breath noise, and a labium offset borrowed from the recorder. D6 alone also has the jet swing limit. It models the paper's metered-air rig, not a player: the bore holds breath, but each note's mouth pressure comes from the paper's dry-air flow, and there is no tonguing, breath or finger motion.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a forced Bickley jet driven by a mouth pressure computed from each note's printed air flow through the card's windway law, with the 1.48 mm flue, acting on a connected duct network

The bore and six finger holes from the same paper, open or closed per its fingering chart, with the open holes' inner radiation matched in series, and the closed pocket behind the flue. The bore's open end reacts as an unflanged thin-walled tube (Garcia Mayen 2021, Eq. 14, via Silva et al. 2009), heard as a baffled monopole

On D5 the tone holes' walls are the paper's 0.3 mm (Davies et al. 2006, Sec. 3): each closed hole, a quarter of one propagation step of the 288 kHz clock, is the lumped shunt of a short closed tube, compliance pi b^2 t/(rho c^2) and inertance rho t/(3 pi b^2) (`duct_node closed-hole`, landed as ac0af0f2c1). Against the 1.5 mm card on one binary it raised D5 by 5.9 c, within 0.2 c of a plane-wave estimate, and moved the pitch gap to the recording from 19.9 to 14.0 c and the mean miss of H2 to H12 from 10.00 to 9.96 dB. No end correction is added: the closed hole's matching volume (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012, Eq. 8), 42 to 77 % of t on these holes, is left out, so each hole's compliance is 0.56 to 0.70 of its value with it

On the other seven pages the tone holes' walls are the paper's 0.3 mm too (2026-11-11): E5, F#5, G5, A5, B5, C#6 and D6 are rendered from cards with each closed hole the lumped shunt and each open hole's chimney 0.3 mm, in place of the 1.5 mm stand-in that G5, B5 and D6 carried (E5, F#5, A5 and C#6 had no page before). On one binary (the lp1 build, sha256 e9d30c4e00e87423, whose byte control, the live G5 card re-rendered on a copy of it, equals the earlier render) the played notes rose 17.91, 19.47, 23.34, 26.24, 25.50, 30.77 and 6.25 c against each card's 1.5 mm twin, and the engine's passive first mode (passive_served.py on each render's own sidecar, each closed hole as its closed stub tube) rose 18.51, 20.08, 23.92, 26.72, 27.10, 33.37 and 6.85 c. The jet term, the played note minus the passive first mode, is -0.46, +10.15, -3.13, +2.18, -15.05, -6.89 and -9.52 c on the 1.5 mm cards and moves by at most 2.6 c with the walls. Against the earlier grade the loose count of B5 went from 4 of 12 to 3 of 12 (the spectral centroid left the spread); G5 and D6 kept theirs, and E5, F#5, A5 and C#6 are graded for the first time, against the neighbouring notes of the same pack

The window's acoustic mass from its own 3-D wall cut, and its radiation from the outer face of the head's cylinder, that radiation's memory stepped exactly with the flow held over each step (27631e7a4)
The contraction loss at the flue exit (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I, vena-contracta coefficient 0.6)
Jet spreading by Fletcher 1976, a trial here: this flue is outside its measured 0.25 to 1.0 mm
A labium offset of 0.203 mm, 0.1374 flue heights, borrowed from the recorder (Bouterse 2010), because no printed whistle value was found. It gives the even harmonics a level at all

Breath noise at the window edge (Verge 1995): gain 1.3e-3 of the jet's dynamic pressure, opening at a flue Reynolds number of 700 (p. 196), through an order-two Butterworth band-pass; with the whole row removed (2026-11-11, the G5 and D6 cards on one binary) the grader's harmonics-to-noise ratio of the clip rises from 50.30 to 60.83 dB on G5 and from 44.08 to 75.53 dB on D6, and the between-harmonic floor in the third octave at 2263 Hz on G5 falls from -53.4 to -70.7 dB re the tone and at 898 Hz on D6 from -46.7 to -91.2 dB, so the row sets most of the between-harmonic floor from about 450 Hz up (on G5 a floor near -61 dB at 713 Hz remains without it); the eight real notes carry 24.7 to 52.1 dB more between-harmonic energy than the renders in that measure (harmonics-to-noise ratio 1.5 to 25.9 dB against 44.1 to 53.6 dB), largest at 224 to 898 Hz on six of the eight notes and at 2263 Hz on the other two; no measured whistle-flue noise level was found in an open source, so the card keeps Verge's value from a recorder-like pipe; and the previews cannot separate the player's breath from the codec, being digitally silent between the notes, with no floor to subtract

On D6 only, a limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, applied in time this model's own way. It lets the first harmonic lead on that note. On D5, G5 and B5 it makes the match worse, so it stays off

In the bore, the player's breath (the shared woodwind pack: Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969, Fletcher and Rossing sec. 8.1, saturated at 27 C with 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 dry), with gas-derived viscothermal loss on the bore's 7 sections, its memory stepped exactly with the flow held over each step (adbb97dbb and f78078db2); the room's dry air at 20 C outside the bore, and Stokes-Kirchhoff air along the path to the receiver
A physical receiver 1 m above the window, summing every open aperture, with the compact radiation load declared valid to 2.8 kHz
physics_missing: A whistle of this make to grade against: the graded notes are a Waltons D whistle's, one short note each from lossy previews; each preview also holds a held take of the same note (about 1 s), and the repo's screen marks the held take invalid for the noise-floor test (no lead-in before the onset, no stationary tail), so it does not rule, so only neighbouring notes rule and nothing has a same-note ruler. The rows below that compare with the recording or the real whistle were measured against the earlier clip, a Sweetone D whistle's slurred scale cut between the slurs (Mirjam Plas, Escola Superior de Musica de Catalunya, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0), which compares only in its held sound. A second whistle's scale differs from it by 3 to 17 dB on single harmonics, so one recording doesn't fix a target closer than that

Pitch: with the paper's 0.3 mm walls the notes sound D5 +9.1, E5 -4.8, F#5 -15.4, G5 -0.7, A5 -4.6, B5 +4.6, C#6 +5.4 and D6 +13.0 c from A440 equal temperament. The bore's gas is the player's breath, which lifts every note about 11 c over the paper's dry air at 20 C (the G5 page measured +10.68 c; the other notes' share was not measured), so against the paper's own gas the notes would sit about 11 c lower. F#5 stays 15.4 c flat of its name: its passive first mode is 24.9 c flat of equal temperament and its jet term, the played note minus that mode, is +9.5 c, and nothing on the card says why. The paper prints one frequency (D5 = 587 Hz at 6.2 l/min), so the tempered notes of the other seven are an assumption, not a measurement. The jet term runs from -16.7 c (B5) to +9.5 c (F#5) across the eight notes; what sets it from note to note is not separated. No pressure was chosen to correct any of it

The real whistle's spectrum: on D5, G5 and B5, H2 is 31 to 35 dB under H1, against 17 to 25 on this whistle, and H5 stands 15 to 33 dB over it. On D6, H3 is -3.4 dB re H1 against -27, and H2 stands well over this whistle's

A jet drive from print that works here. Refused on these notes: the Auvray 2014 jet drive (wrong note on 10 of 11 whistle notes), the Ernoult-Fabre window mass, the unsteady windway with the forced jet, and the de la Cuadra 2005 exit law, whose Reynolds range excludes this flue. The momentum drive of Thwaites and Fletcher 1983 silences B5 and D6 and moves G5 to its third mode
A player: no tonguing, breath or finger motion. The bore holds breath, but each note's mouth pressure comes from the paper's dry-air flow and is not recomputed for breath

Release: in the scale each note's output reaches digital silence 0.14 to 0.19 s after its release starts, so nothing rings beyond that. Against the earlier slurred scale only the held sound could be compared; the graded short notes compare the attack as well
Overblown notes: none are posted. Only the paper's measured operating points were rendered, so where each register begins and any hysteresis are unmapped

The flue's true taper, the pocket's shape, hole shape and undercut, and the bore's narrowing at the wedge. Where the wedge tip sits in the wall isn't published, and the cards use one end of that bracket

The paper's 0.3 mm hole wall on B5, G5 and D6 was first tried (2026-11-10) with the lumped closed hole and 0.3 mm open chimneys, each against its own 1.5 mm card on one binary: B5 moved +25.5 c (pitch gap to the earlier clip 16.2 to 9.3 c) but its mean miss of H2 to H12 grew from 7.85 to 8.72 dB; G5 moved +23.3 c (42.5 to 19.2 c) but its miss grew from 11.39 to 12.10 dB; D6 moved +6.2 c and its gap grew from 1.41 to 4.83 c. Each got worse on one of those two figures, and the three pages kept 1.5 mm under the rule that both had to be no worse. On 2026-11-11 the walls replaced the stand-in on all three under the owner's order that a value the paper prints replaces a stand-in whatever the count does
A measured jet card: these cards use the repository's interim one

Openings that hear each other: the open holes and the end radiate apart. Tried with every opening hearing every other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), which is passive here because the side holes carry baffled loads, the row lowered B5, D6 and G5 by 1.74, 0.13 and 1.81 c on the raw renders. All three already sit flat of the recording (16.2, 1.41 and 42.5 c), so the gap grew, to 17.9, 1.54 and 44.3 c. The mean miss of H2 to H12 re H1 against the recording's held part moved 7.85 to 7.81 dB on B5, 15.105 to 15.114 on D6 and 11.39 to 11.12 on G5. Weighted instead by the two openings' own radiation resistances (`outlet_mutual pritchard`, Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1, as the flute's D4 and G4 pages carry it) and rendered on one binary, each page beside its own card without the row (2026-11-10), B5, D6 and G5 fell 3.54, 0.18 and 3.56 c and played 0.331, 0.020 and 0.385 dB quieter, so the gap grew again, to 19.7, 1.59 and 46.1 c, and the mean miss moved 7.85 to 7.71 dB on B5, 15.111 to 15.215 on D6 and 11.39 to 10.89 on G5. The pages and the scale and melody stops keep the openings apart; D5, with only the end open, has nothing to pair

Separated flow at the openings: the flow leaving each open hole and the open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). Tried with C_c 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. Every page rendered. The row lowered B5, D5, D6 and G5 by 1.13, 0.08, 0.07 and 0.25 c on the raw renders. All four already sit flat of the recording (16.2, 19.9, 1.41 and 42.5 c), so the gap grew, to 17.3, 20.0, 1.48 and 42.8 c. The mean miss of H2 to H12 re H1 against the recording's held part moved 7.85 to 7.32 dB on B5, 10.00 to 9.77 on D5, 15.11 to 15.25 on D6 and 11.39 to 10.62 on G5. No page gains on both, so the row stays off

The player's airway (`upstream_airway`, the row the flute's C5, D4 and G4 pages carry): tried on all four pages, each beside its live card on one binary. The lungs supply the paper's blowing pressure plus the airway's steady drop (3.60 to 5.87 % of it), so the developing windway, judged again at that foot pressure, holds the paper's pressure, within 0.0004 Pa of the live page's. The pitch gap to the recording grew on every page, by 0.06 to 0.17 c, so no page carries the row. Its airway is Weibel's tree (Saab et al. 2021, Story 2008) with the voice cards' stand-in wall. On D5 with the 0.3 mm hole walls it was tried again, beside that card on one binary: the pitch fell 0.135 c, so the gap grew from 14.03 to 14.16 c while the mean miss of H2 to H12 fell from 9.96 to 9.93 dB, and D5 doesn't carry it either

The closed holes' printed matching volume and series length (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012, Eqs. 8 and 34; `matching series` on each `duct_node closed-hole` row): tried on the four 0.3 mm cards, D5's page and the B5, G5 and D6 cards above, each against the same card without the words on one binary. The first realisation of the series length shortened the two bore sections at each closed hole and so took their volume away as well, nearly the hole's own on the largest holes (17.7 against 18.2 mm^3); it moved D5 +2.92, G5 +1.68, B5 +0.57 and D6 +1.93 c, where the paper's terms give +0.63, +0.63, +0.40 and +0.32 c. With that volume given back to the hole's compliance, so that the series length adds only the paper's mass, the moves are +0.67, +0.60, +0.37 and +0.34 c. D5 and G5 then come 0.67 and 0.60 c nearer the recording, but their mean miss of H2 to H12 grows from 9.85 to 9.94 and from 12.10 to 12.13 dB; B5's miss falls from 8.721 to 8.718 dB but its pitch gap grows from 9.30 to 9.67 c; D6 gets worse on both, 4.83 to 5.17 c and 14.96 to 15.00 dB. Each got worse on one of the two figures, so no page carries the words
